After months of hard work and dedication, she finally ________ her degree and walked across the stage to receive her diploma.
questions.solution_en:
The verb in the blank and 'walked' are joined by using 'and'. Here we need to follow parallelism to maintain the structure of the sentence. Since the verb 'walked' is in the simple past tense, 'earned' is the most appropriate choice among the given options.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: After months of hard work and dedication, she finally earned her degree and walked across the stage to receive her diploma.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

If he would have studied harder, / he would have surely / passed the difficult examination.
options_en: If he would have studied harder,
questions.solution_en:
The error is in the structure of the conditional clause in "If he would have studied harder."

This sentence describes an unreal past condition and its probable past result (a Type 3 conditional sentence). The correct structure for the 'if-clause' in such sentences is "If + subject + had + past participle (V3)." The main clause correctly uses "would have + past participle (V3)."

Therefore, "If he would have studied harder" should be "If he had studied harder."

Correct Sentence: If he had studied harder, he would have surely passed the difficult examination.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Note:

· V3 (Past Participle): The past participle form of a verb, often ending in -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n, used in forming perfect tenses and passive voice.

· Conditional Sentences: Sentences expressing factual implications, or hypothetical situations and their consequences. The structure "If + Past Perfect, ... would have + Past Participle" is used for unreal past conditions.

questions.q_en: Describe how you will tell your teacher that the students will have decorated the classroom in passive voice.
options_en: The classroom will have been decorated by the students.
The classroom will be decorated by the students.
The students are decorating the classroom.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb ['been'] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Future Perfect. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Future Perfect.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + will/shall + have + V3 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + will/shall + have been + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case)

For example:

She will have bought the gold. (Active Voice)

The gold will have been bought by her. (Passive Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: "The classroom will have been decorated by the students."

Hence, option (a) is correct.

I couldn't _____ to walk on the hot sand with my ____ feet.

In the first blank, we need a verb that fits in the context of walking on the hot sand. The word "bear" fits this context perfectly and implies that it was difficult for the subject to walk on the hot sand. "Bear" can mean to endure or tolerate something difficult or uncomfortable.

In the second blank, we need an adjective to describe the condition of the feet. The word "bare" means uncovered or naked, which fits in the context of walking on hot sand because one wouldn't want to walk on hot sand with uncovered or naked feet.

"Bares" is incorrect as it is a verb which means "uncovers (a part of the body or other thing) and exposes it to view".

The complete sentence is: I couldn't bear to walk on the hot sand with my bare feet.

Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Shreya said that she was having a sandwich in her breakfast.
options_en: Shreya said, "She was having a sandwich in her breakfast."
Shreya said, "I am having a sandwich in my breakfast."
Shreya said, "She is having a sandwich in her breakfast."
Shreya said, "I was having a sandwich in my breakfast."
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Continuous Tense.

Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Present Continuous (Subject + is/am/are + V1 +ing + Object)

For example:

He said that he was checking the assignment. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I am checking the assignment." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

She - I

Was - am

Her - my

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

Populism is a political strategy that prioritizes the concerns and interests of the general populace over those of the elite. Its emergence is characterized by increased backing for leaders or movements pledging to advocate for the grievances of ordinary citizens. This surge is propelled by several factors, including economic instability, cultural apprehension, and a perceived disconnect between the ruling class and the wider population. Populist leaders frequently employ rhetoric that resonates with disenfranchised individuals, harnessing their dissatisfaction to gain support. While populism can provide a platform for marginalized perspectives, it also presents significant challenges to democratic principles and institutions. Critics argue that populist movements often oversimplify intricate issues, promote divisive narratives, and weaken the essential checks and balances of democratic governance. Consequently, comprehending the ascent of populism necessitates a nuanced examination of its socio-economic and political foundations.

The word "surge" refers to a sudden and powerful increase or rise in something, such as a sudden rush or movement forward. 'Rise' means an increase in amount, number, value, or quality. So, the two words can be used as synonyms of each other. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

Slump - a sudden severe or prolonged fall in the price, value, or amount of something.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. This has an impact not just on global poverty, but also on Indians' awareness of the country's poverty for the first time in a decade.

B. And, for the first time in a decade, this update includes India's poverty data.

C. From 15 September 2022, a new global poverty line has been established, with the World Bank revising its data in the Poverty and Inequality Platform on this basis.

D. According to Sunitha Sinha, Roy and Roy van der Weide of the World Bank's Policy Research Working Paper, "poverty in India had dropped over the recent decade, although not as much as previously thought."
questions.solution_en: The correct order to form a coherent paragraph is CBAD. Sentence C comes first as it introduces the establishment of a new global poverty line by the World Bank, indicating a significant update in poverty measurement methodology. Sentence B highlights a specific aspect of the update: the inclusion of India's poverty data. This is noteworthy because it marks the first time in ten years that India's poverty data is being incorporated into the updated metrics. After introducing the update and its inclusion of India's poverty data, sentence A discusses the broader implications of this change. It suggests that the update has a dual impact: it affects global poverty measurements and also increases awareness among Indians about their country's poverty situation after a decade-long absence of updated data. Sentence D provides further context by citing specific research findings. It mentions the observations of experts from the World Bank, who note that poverty in India has decreased over the recent decade, albeit not as significantly as previously believed. This adds depth to the discussion and supports the earlier statements about the significance of the update. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Could you please remind to me to attend the team meeting tomorrow at 10 AM, so I don't forget to join the virtual call and contribute to the discussion on the latest project updates and upcoming deadlines?
questions.solution_en:
'To' should not be used with some verbs when followed by an object. Such verbs are- advise, welcome, ask, warm, forbid, order, remind, compliment, etc. So, drop 'to' from 'remind to me'. Also, modal verbs are followed by a base form of verbs so the use of third person singular 'reminds' is incorrect. Therefore, 'remind me to attend' is the right phrase here.

The correct sentence is - "Could you please remind me to attend the team meeting tomorrow at 10 AM, so I don't forget to join the virtual call and contribute to the discussion on the latest project updates and upcoming deadlines?"

Hence, option (c) is correct.

Note:

Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Here 'can' expresses the ability of the person to speak (main verb) Spanish. This ability cannot be expressed by the main verb 'speak'.

Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

The scenic hill town of Darjeeling is famous for its 3T's - Tea, Timber, and Tourists. Originally established as a British sanatorium, it quickly earned the nickname 'Queen of Hills' and has become a popular tourist spot. The charming town welcomes visitors with stunning landscapes, drifting clouds, and pleasant weather. However, the other side of this hill station is marked by the struggles of Darjeeling's residents, who face challenges with basic water and sanitation services. Darjeeling has become synonymous with water scarcity, still depending on the water supply system set up by the British government between 1910 and 1915 for just 10,000 residents. However, the city's current population is around 118,805. This unexpected growth has posed a major challenge in the proper planning and installation of crucial municipal services like water and sewage systems. The city presents a dual effect, offering increased options for accommodating tourists, while also raising concerns about the capacity of the city to absorb this rampant growth and the pressure it exerts on municipal services. Darjeeling is located on a landscape with uneven layers, leading most homes to depend on stacked stairs and narrow, slippery paths for access. The electric wires and water pipelines are intertwined, demonstrating a harmonious coexistence that highlights a symbiotic relationship between fire and water elements. In Darjeeling, people usually throw household waste into the jhoras (drains going down the hill). Jhoras are local stormwater drains or flood harvesting systems that play a vital role in managing excess water during storms. Similar to the Aahar Pynes in Bihar and Nullahs in the northern regions, these systems help to prevent flooding and protect the local environment. This drain, among others, leads to one of the most visited sites, RockVille Garden, a picturesque tourist location known for its natural waterfall. The mismanaged disposal of waste has further exacerbated the problem of solid waste, creating a mountain of waste amid the scenic Eastern Himalayan mountain range.

What role do jhoras play in Darjeeling's infrastructure?
options_en: They are used as community hubs for commerce.
They are used for channelling and managing surplus water.
They offer scenic attractions featuring natural landscapes.
questions.solution_en: The passage mentions, 'Jhoras are local stormwater drains or flood harvesting systems that play a vital role in managing excess water during storms.' This indicates that their primary function is to channel and manage surplus water, helping to prevent flooding. The passage does not describe jhoras as community hubs, residential structures or scenic attractions. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en: Select the option with the correct use of future tense.
options_en: In March, my brother will have been saving money for his world tour for exactly two years.
In March, my brother will be saved money for his world tour for exactly two years.
In March, my brother will have saving money for his world tour for exactly two years.
In March, my brother will have save money for his world tour for exactly two years.
questions.solution_en:
The correct option is a).

This sentence correctly uses the future perfect continuous tense (will have been + present participle). This tense is ideal here because it focuses on the duration ("for exactly two years") of an activity (saving money) that will continue up to a specific point in the future ("In March").

· Option (b): This uses an incorrect passive construction ("will be saved"). "My brother" (the subject) is the one performing the action ("saving money"), so the active voice is needed.

· Option (c): This is grammatically incorrect. The structure "will have" should be followed by a past participle, but here it is followed by a present participle ("saving") without the necessary "been."

· Option (d): This is grammatically incorrect. "will have" must be followed by a past participle, not the base form of the verb ("save").

Note: Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).
questions.solution_hi:
The correct option is a).

This sentence correctly uses the future perfect continuous tense (will have been + present participle). This tense is ideal here because it focuses on the duration ("for exactly two years") of an activity (saving money) that will continue up to a specific point in the future ("In March").

· Option (b): This uses an incorrect passive construction ("will be saved"). "My brother" (the subject) is the one performing the action ("saving money"), so the active voice is needed.

· Option (c): This is grammatically incorrect. The structure "will have" should be followed by a past participle, but here it is followed by a present participle ("saving") without the necessary "been."

· Option (d): This is grammatically incorrect. "will have" must be followed by a past participle, not the base form of the verb ("save").

Note: Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

questions.q_en:
Substitute the underlined word-segment with most appropriate idiom.

Everyone knew about his impending resignation, but it remained the obvious unaddressed problem during the entire meeting.
questions.solution_en:
The phrase "the obvious unaddressed problem" refers to a significant issue that everyone is aware of but no one discusses, often due to discomfort or sensitivity.

The idiom "the elephant in the room" means an obvious major problem or controversial issue that is conspicuously present but avoided as a subject for discussion. This perfectly describes the situation with his unmentioned resignation.

Therefore, it is the most suitable idiomatic replacement.

a) a fish out of water - someone who is uncomfortable in a particular or unfamiliar situation. (Describes a person's feeling, not an unaddressed issue.)

c) a wolf in sheep's clothing - a dangerous person who pretends to be harmless. (Describes a deceptive person, not an undiscussed topic.)

d) a storm in a teacup - a lot of unnecessary anger and worry about a matter that is not important. (Suggests the issue is trivial, which is not implied here.)

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The announcement was made to coincide with Respect for the Aged Day - a national holiday in Japan.

B. Two Japanese sisters have been certified by Guinness World Records as the world's oldest living identical twins at over 107 years and 300 days.

C. Umeno and Koume, both described as sociable people, were born on 5 November 1913 on Shodoshima island.

D. Umeno Sumiyama and Koume Kodama have broken the record set by late Japanese twin sisters Kin Narita and Gin Kanie.
questions.solution_en:
A triplet BDC would be formed because B tells that two Japanese sisters have been certified as the world's oldest living identical twins, D tells Umeno Sumiyama and Koume Kodama are those two sisters, and then C provides more information about those two sisters. Lastly, A would end the passage by stating that the announcement regarding the same was made on 'Respect for the Aged Day'.

Thus, the final order is BDCA.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

____ the big fight is between Facebook and Twitter, the performance of WhatsApp will be keenly watched.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence intends to convey despite the fact that the big fight is between Facebook and Twitter, WhatsApp's performance will be watched. The correct conjunction to be used is 'though'. It is one of the subordinating conjunctions which instead of joining two independent clauses of equal importance, make one clause less important than another. Rest of the conjunctions are also subordinating but their usage varies. 'Just as' is used to connect things on similar theme, 'if when is used to convey condition with time and 'before' is used to convey in advance of the time of some event.

Hence, option (b) is correct.
